A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRIDENT research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched despite added material and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-property classification experiments and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix E, including AMES and hERG results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional classification and regression results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The HTA construction procedure, tri-modal encoders, volume-based global objective, functional-group local alignment and momentum integration are unchanged. Sections 3 and Appendix B retain the same method and algorithms.

E1.justification: v2 adds ESOL, FreeSolv, Lipophilicity and Caco-2 regression, plus CYP P450 2C19 inhibition classification. Counting AMES and hERG already evaluated in v1's appendix, coverage expands from 13 to 18 datasets and extends beyond classification to continuous-property prediction. The pretraining corpus is unchanged.

E2.justification: MolXPT, BioT5 and BioT5+ are added to the existing DILI, Carcinogens and Skin Reaction comparisons in Table 2 and the AMES/hERG comparison in v2 Table 9. Uni-Mol is additionally evaluated in the new regression comparison, Table 8. This substantially broadens the comparator set; Table 1's membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added regression experiments introduce RMSE evaluation alongside the existing classification metrics. The stated scaffold-split protocol, retained dataset settings, encoder configurations and Appendix B training configuration remain unchanged; no rerun or protocol revision is established for the existing experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 3 and Tables 3–4 retain the same component and loss-integration ablations. The raw-JSON versus LLM-summary and tri-modal versus concatenation studies already appear in v1 Tables 9–10 and are retained as v2 Tables 11–12. The added benchmark evaluations introduce no new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and report means and standard deviations, with the same standard-deviation definition in Appendix B. The new results follow that practice, and the added checklist merely restates it. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or increased run counts are reported.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 8 and 10 add substantial result sets for the five new datasets, including TRIDENT (M-M) RMSE of 0.72±0.07 on ESOL and 1.42±0.03 on FreeSolv. Tables 2 and 9 add scores for three new comparators on retained tasks. Matched pre-existing results remain unchanged; Table 1's averages changing from 78.3/78.5 to 78.28/78.46 are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The volume definition, alignment objectives, pooling expressions, momentum update and metric equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the state-of-the-art performance claim from 11 to 18 downstream tasks. The methodological contributions and novelty claims are retained. This update is incomplete: the introduction's contribution list and conclusion still claim 11 tasks.

C2.justification: Appendix E.1 newly interprets regression results as evidence that TRIDENT applies to continuous-property prediction, while E.2 extends the TDC generalization discussion across classification and regression. Existing explanations of HTA, alignment and summarization benefits, and the limitation concerning molecular targets and metabolites, are retained.

D1.justification: v2's abstract newly supplies a repository address for code and data. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time information in Appendix B are unchanged. The added checklist still says release will occur upon acceptance, leaving actual availability unresolved within the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the four new baselines, HAGE, GOBERT and two molecular self-training papers, and removes the causal-subgraph and instruction-aware image-retrieval citations. Section 2.2 locally expands its bioinformatics discussion, while the central positioning relative to GRAM and existing molecule-text models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the evaluation and baseline paragraphs, adds a regression subsection in Appendix E, and includes acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. Author and conference text also change. The main section sequence, method exposition and most appendix prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds result Tables 8 and 10, expands comparator and dataset rows in existing tables, and relocates the retained appendix ablation tables. It also reformats the author block, resizes Figure 4 and adjusts text wrapping around Table 4. Figures 1–3 and the overall visual organization are retained.

improvement.justification: The added regression evaluations and broader comparisons on retained TDC tasks strengthen evidence for TRIDENT's applicability beyond v1's classification-only evaluation. The benefit is meaningful but limited by incomplete documentation updates: the abstract's 18-task claim conflicts with retained 11-task statements, and the repository announcement conflicts with the checklist's release-upon-acceptance statement.
